title: DNA Replication Fork Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: college placement Biology
description: Interactive diagram overlay showing the complete enzymatic machinery at a DNA replication fork, with Explore and Quiz modes for 13 labeled structures.

learningObjectives: Identify the enzymes at the replication fork and state their functions
Explain why leading strand synthesis is continuous while lagging strand synthesis is discontinuous
Describe the roles of primase, DNA Pol I, and DNA Ligase in Okazaki fragment processing

keyQuestions: Why can't DNA Polymerase III start a new strand without a primer?
Why is the lagging strand synthesized as Okazaki fragments?
What would happen if DNA Ligase were absent?
commonMisconceptions: Helicase breaks covalent bonds (it breaks hydrogen bonds)
The leading and lagging strands use different enzymes (they use the same Pol III)
Okazaki fragments are caused by pausing (they result from 5' to 3' directionality constraint)
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz mode identification of all 13 structures
